# Goals for this script:

**1. Brief introduction to the quarto `qmd` format.  **

* Quarto enables you to weave together content and executable code into a finished document.  
* To learn more about Quarto see <https://quarto.org>.  

**2. Quick data handling exercise**  


---  

## Running Code

When you click the **Render** button a document will be generated that includes both content and the output of embedded code. You can embed code like this:

```{r}
1 + 1
```

The `#| echo: false` option (placed on the first line of the chunk) disables the printing of code (only output is displayed).

```{r}
#| echo: false
1 + 1
```



--- 

$\LaTeX$ can be implemented the same way as in `Rmd` files:

* `$y_t = \beta_0 + \beta_1 x_t + \varepsilon_t$`  
* generates  
* $y_t = \beta_0 + \beta_1 x_t + \varepsilon_t$ 


--- 

#### Map plotting:

- Again, similar to Markdown, with added features  



```{r}
#| label: fig-NCarea
#| fig-cap: "NC Counties: area"
#| warning: false

library(sf)
library(ggplot2)

nc <- sf::st_read(system.file("shape/nc.shp", package = "sf"), quiet = TRUE)
ggplot(nc) +
  geom_sf(aes(fill = AREA))
```


Using the `#|label: NCarea` handle, you can reference the figure in your text, by includig `@fig-NCarea` cross-reference. For example: 

* @fig-NCarea shows the area of each county in North Carolina.

#  Quick data handling exercise

```{r}
library(tidyr)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)

Stocks <- read.csv("data/Stocks.csv")
Stocks$time <- as.Date(Stocks$time)
summary(Stocks)
head(Stocks,20)
summary(as.factor(Stocks$stock))
```

**Tasks**

**Starting from long-format data frame, prepare the data & run OLS estimation**


1. Use the following data range: 1980-Jan to 1989-Dec.

2. Drop "crsp" stock from the dataset

3. Plot the data using ggplot2

4. Generate first lags of stock returns (use dplyr functionality to create the lagged variables before you convert the dataset to a wide format for estimation in Step 5)

5. Use OLS to estimate the following model:

$\text{ibm}_t = \beta_0 + \beta_1 \text{ibm}_{t-1} + \beta_2 \text{mobil}_{t-1} + \beta_3 \text{ge}_{t-1} + \varepsilon_t$
